directive.thread_id: port-contract gate lane 2026-11-03: the runner a cloud session loads
directive.quote: Move the list-reading part of ai-command-center's hook-dispatch.py, and the judge start, into a Workshop tool. Move it byte for byte. Change only the address it reads from: make that a DATA value instead of the hardcoded 127.0.0.1:8788.

targets.baseline_commit_message: check-every-tool-call: the hook dispatcher's check-list reader and its choosing and answering, moved byte for byte

preserve: Off only on an exact "Off"; a missing row, an unreadable list, a failed refresh or a missing snapshot all mean on
a failed refresh keeps the previous snapshot and says why beside it; the snapshot is replaced whole
the tool call never waits for the door once a snapshot exists: refreshing is a detached process
a row marked Off still runs while honour_off is false, and the mark is said
the door's address and how its key is read are the caller's settings; the key is read at refresh time and sent only in the Authorization header
allowed_deltas: a run verb (run_the_check_list): a session with no other copy of the rows reads them from the snapshot and runs the rows that name workshop_run, picked and answered by guard_rows.py
the door's address may come from the environment variable door.url_from names, so a repository's files need not name anyone's door

the check rows (record:check, read with the door's where { kind: check }, kept as checks in the snapshot): run judges the call against the rows whose kinds name its unit kind (git-commit, git-push by the same command match a hook-guard row's acts_on uses, else tool-call) through check_rows.judge, the one judge
banned_substitutions: a second reader of the check rows
a door address written in code
_paths: The source lives in a private repository, so it is named by the BLAKE3 identity of its path (path_multihash); a checkout of that repository beside this one finds it.
